results.content: Treating 150–300 ms as election time. It’s the paper’s example election timeout. etcd’s default is 1,000 ms, drawn from 1,000 to 1,900, and measured failover took 1.1 to 1.9 seconds.

results.title: Raft Explained: Leader Election, Log Replication, and Safety
results.content: The Raft consensus algorithm explained: raft leader election with randomized timeouts, raft log replication through a strong leader, and the raft safety properties that keep etcd, Consul, and CockroachDB consistent.

results.title: Raft Consensus Algorithm — Leader Election and Log Replication
results.content: The election timeout is randomized (typically 150–300 ms) to avoid split votes where many candidates start simultaneously. If a split vote occurs, all candidates time out and start a new election.

results.title: Understanding Leader Election in RAFT consensus mechanism
results.content: Election Timeout: The time a follower waits without a heartbeat before assuming the leader has failed and starting an election. It’s randomized (e.g., 150–300 ms) to prevent simultaneous elections.

results.title: Leader Election Explained — Bully, Ring, Raft, lease-based
results.content: Raft's default heartbeat interval is around 50–150 ms; the election timeout is randomised between 150 ms and 300 ms; an election itself completes in another round-trip.

results.title: Leader Election and Terms — padho-wiki
results.content: The Raft paper recommends 150-300 ms with heartbeats every ~50 ms, which gives a 3-6× safety factor over the heartbeat interval.t=60 ms. N1's heartbeat would have gone out; doesn't reach anyone. t=150 ms - 300 ms. Each of N2-N5 has a randomized election deadline.

results.title: Wesley Aptekar-Cassels | How Raft Works
results.content: Follower nodes have a randomized "election timeout" (the paper suggests using rand(150ms, 300ms)). If the election timeout elapses without the follower receiving a heartbeat from a leader, the follower will convert into a candidate.
